# SK1051 — Simplify the pattern

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A run of `not` that cancels itself, or a `not` in front of a relational pattern that the operator already spells.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | 9.0 |
| Since | 1.3 |
| ReSharper | `DoubleNegationInPattern` (`resharper_double_negation_in_pattern_highlighting`) |

## Why

Patterns compose, so they also accumulate. `SK1011` and `SK1014` introduce property and relational patterns and nothing tidies them afterwards, which is how a modernization rule creates its own debt: a `not` added to an existing `not` during a refactor, or a `not (> 5)` written because the condition it replaced was `!(x > 5)`. Neither survives being read aloud, and both have an exact spelling that does.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if (value is not not > 0) {
}

if (count is not (> 5)) {
}
```

Write:

```csharp
if (value is > 0) {
}

if (count is <= 5) {
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **`not (> 5)` is `<= 5` only where the type's order is total, which is why this rule is `Semantic` rather than the `Syntax` its proposal assumed.** On `double`, `NaN > 5` is false, so `not (> 5)` matches `NaN` and `<= 5` does not; on `int?`, `not (> 5)` matches `null` and `<= 5` does not. Both rewrites look like De Morgan's law and neither is one, so the inversion is admitted only for a non-nullable `sbyte`/`byte`/`short`/`ushort`/`int`/`uint`/`long`/`ulong`/`char`/`decimal`/`nint`/`nuint` or an enum, and the input type is read from the `is` operand or the governing expression of the `switch` — a `not` inside a property subpattern or a list pattern is declined because the walk cannot see what it is being matched against. ⚠ Cancelling a run of `not` is unconditional and needs none of that; only the relational inversion does. ⚠ **The top of a `not` run owns the finding**, so a triple negation is one rewrite rather than two overlapping ones, and an odd residual is folded into the inversion instead of being left for a second pass — a rule that still fires after its own fix turns `skala fix` into a loop. ⚠ **The residual pattern keeps whatever parentheses it had**: `not` binds tighter than `and`, so unwrapping `Z and not not (A or B)` would produce `Z and A or B`, a different predicate. ⚠ Not covered: `RedundantIsBeforeRelationalPattern`, `ReplaceObjectPatternWithVarPattern`, `ExtractCommonPropertyPattern` and `ReplaceSequenceEqualWithConstantPattern`, each of which is a different rewrite with its own proof obligation.
